_spec.purpose: The variety engine. No two decks visually alike.
_spec.why: Each run records the techniques, palette, structure and camera it used, and the next run reads this to know what it may not reach for again. Without it a machine converges on whatever worked once, which is how a daily product develops a house style nobody chose.
_spec.enforced_by: scripts/carousel/bespoke_check.py measures WITHIN a deck. This ledger constrains ACROSS decks. Both are needed: a deck can be nine different drawings that all look like last Tuesday.

entries.rebuilt_at_the_ninth_pass: Three techniques in this list named frames that were replaced during scoring and were caught by two judges reading the ledger against the renders. Slide 7 was recorded as a redaction field of struck bars, which is a drawing nobody made: two judges read the struck bars as an assertion that something had been struck out, which c17 does not support, and it was rebuilt as the survey title block its own dossier had asked for. Slide 3 was recorded as a flat field of identical cells and was rebuilt under one raking key, because a flat frame reads as an unfinished render and its own risks list said so. Slide 6 ran its courses DOWN, which forced four display words to 90 degrees under four near-black plates, and now runs them across. The ledger is the next run's only memory of what not to reuse, so a technique recorded here that never shipped blocks tomorrow from a drawing nobody made and leaves the drawing that ran unrecorded. This entry is now written against the renders rather than against the plan.

value.note: THE FRAMES WERE REDRAWN AND THEN THE PLAN WAS CORRECTED, and both halves are recorded because the second one is the finding. The first build measured a deck median of 4.1 against a plan of 20, which is nine near-black rectangles. The plane source kept its shape and gained the amplitude it always needed, reaching 10.4. What then held it under 20 was the SCRIMS the 4.5 contrast floor required under six frames' type, and a scrim necessarily darkens the frame it saves. THEN THE SCRIMS WERE MEASURED PROPERLY AND FOUR OF THEM WERE TOO BIG. Frames 1, 2, 6 and 7 carried reserves sized by eye rather than by the type they protect, and frame 1's ran 115px past anything it was holding up, so the frame that introduces the light-from-below law had its darkest band at the bottom. Derived per lowest contiguous type run the deck came back to 11.4 with every line still clearing 4.5, which says the reserves were never the whole cost. Some of it was an unmeasured number nobody had checked.

bespoke.note: The median ROSE from 0.3091 to 0.395 when the four oversized scrims came off, because letting the plenum wash read at the foot of every frame is itself a shared vocabulary. That is a real cost of the right fix and it is recorded rather than smoothed over. 4 and 9 were the closest pair before the change and both judges named them, so the change did not create the pair, it raised the floor under all of them.

avoid_next: FIXING THE LOUD INSTANCE OF A DEFECT LEAVES THE QUIET ONE BESIDE IT. A judge found allocation_routes() returning len() over a typed three-element list, under a comment swearing the count was never a typed 3. It was repaired carefully, with a post mortem written into the docstring. The SAME judge found in the next round that verified_count, ten lines below that docstring, was len() over a typed ONE-element list. The repair had been scoped to the string the finding named. When a defect is a CLASS, grep the file for the class before calling it fixed.

MEASURE BEFORE RECORDING A REASON FOR NOT FIXING SOMETHING. Round 3 declined the scrim work and wrote an arithmetic justification beside it, that derived scrims come out larger on six of nine frames. The next round's judge re-derived it off this deck's own render_report and showed the opposite: per lowest contiguous type run they come out SMALLER on five. The deferral was still right, for a different reason, which is that re-lighting seven frames against a contrast floor late in a run is how a shipping deck turns red. A right decision with a wrong reason attached is worse than no reason, because the next run inherits the reason and stops looking.

PLAN THE TYPE RESERVES BEFORE THE VALUE ARC, NOT AFTER. This deck planned a median of 20, relit once to reach it, and then lost the difference again to the scrims its own contrast floor required under six frames. A dark register cannot hold a mid arc AND clear 4.5 on type over art unless the reserves are in the plan from the start. Decide where the type sits and what holds it up, then set the arc from what is left.

EVERY DRAWN HOLE NEEDS THREE VALUES FROM THE FIRST RENDER. The deck declared a structural law that a hole is a body with a lit lip, a side wall and a floor, capped it to two frames, and then drew flat black squares on four. A judge found it and the repair fixed all four. The law was right and the execution did not follow it, which is the shape plan_render_check exists for and cannot see, because it compares STRINGS rather than geometry.

A PROBE THAT TAKES A MAX PIXEL WILL FIRE ON THE LAW BEING KEPT. Three of this deck's own acceptance probes threw during repairs and all three were faults in the measurement: a cavity sampled mostly off the frame edge, an ABSOLUTE bloom threshold that only measured bleed while the ground was near black, and a max-pixel test above a boundary that fired the moment every punched hole gained the lit lip the deck's own law requires. Write a region test when the claim is about a region.

A PLACE WAS IN THE SNAPSHOTS THE WHOLE TIME AND NOBODY LOOKED UNTIL ROUND FOUR. Two judges charged the deck for naming no Texas place and the answer given twice was that no claim carried one. That was true of the claims and false of the SOURCES: the Horizon guide says in its own words that the machine goes in a new 20 MW data center with advanced liquid cooling in Round Rock, Texas, in a file this run had already fetched and stored. It took a third asking to go and read it. The lesson is not 'fetch a source that carries a place', it is GREP THE SNAPSHOTS YOU ALREADY HAVE BEFORE CONCLUDING THERE IS NO PLACE IN THE STORY. And the place that shipped is still the wrong one for the subject: Round Rock is in Williamson County and belongs to the successor, while the machine that closes sits in Travis County and is never located on any frame.

THE DEDUPE GATE DOES NOT COMPARE INSTRUMENT. Deck 14 was a Texas university supercomputer whose own docs restrict access and so is this one, four days apart, and dedupe_check cleared it at 0.35 because it compares topic, entities and keywords. Two judges read it as the same story twice. An `instrument` field on this ledger, compared across the window, is the upgrade that would catch it.

FRAME 5 WAS THE THINNEST FRAME AND ITS OWN RISK NOTE PREDICTED IT. The note said a mostly empty dark frame can read as unfinished art rather than an unfinished install, and named the mitigation, which was to draw the punch column at full fidelity to the top edge. The column stopped below the headline. A risk note that names its own mitigation should be read back against the render before the frame is called done.

entries.register: BROAD DAYLIGHT ON THE GULF COASTAL PRAIRIE, the first outdoor deck of the eighteen. One declared sun at 34 degrees governs slides 6 and 7 and every object throws from it. There is no interior, no emission, no document-as-paper and no artificial light anywhere. Value comes from Lake Charles clay at two depths, so no shadow in the deck reaches black.
techniques: one-point perspective relief on the cover, soffit, wall, doorway and every slab joint converging on a vanishing point off the right edge, with the saw-cut joints drawn BEFORE the cast so the shadow darkens them rather than sitting under them
a hachure phenology ramp whose position along it is days elapsed at 4.3602 px per day, so the ramp IS the seven month calendar rather than a gradient placed by eye
a horizontal domain warp over a distant live oak motte line, which is the only element in the band with an edge a horizontal displacement can move
two runs of the same ground in plan-oblique, each crossed by a hard cast edge at a computed fraction of its OWN length, so a proportion is drawn without a scale and no ratio can be read between them
a slope chart staked as a lit plywood board, with the axis anchored at zero, the zero printed, and the confidence intervals drawn at true scale with caps at their own bounds
two dissimilar solids at ONE height under ONE sun, throwing one shadow length because they are the same height rather than because the light moved between them
a cumulus occlusion on a 27 degree diagonal with the penumbra feathered on BOTH sides of the terminator, and footpath ruts holding the deck's darkest values
a flow field of wind-laid grass advected on a declared onshore wind, run identically inside a staked traverse and outside it, so an absence is drawn as a measurement
a benchmark monument on open prairie, a mark set down so a LATER survey can be taken from it, which is what a prospective evaluation is

entries.light_deck_note: THE CAP BINDS AND THIS DECK BREACHES IT, and unlike deck 14 this run CHOSE the register knowing so. deck_median_L is 71.1 against LIGHT_L 60.0, and the eight run window still holds deck 14 at 73.1. check_register does NOT fail, because deck 14's named waiver subtracts it and leaves over = 1, which is the exact effect deck 14's own light_deck_note says a waiver must never have. So the brand rule is broken behind a green gate. Deck 14's avoid_next is addressed to this deck by name and says do not reach for a light ground again until the counted window holds none. It held one. Two of three judges marked variety down to 5.0 and 5.5 for it and both were right. NO WAIVER IS CLAIMED FOR THIS DATE. It is recorded as a breach.
avoid_next: THE NEXT DECK IS DARK, AND THIS IS A DEBT THIS RUN INCURRED RATHER THAN INHERITED. Deck 14's breach was a plan nobody measured until round 3. This one chose a light register with deck 14 still in the window and wrote the justification into its storyboard, where it miscounted the ledger twice and had to be corrected against the measurements. Draw the next deck in the Big Bend dusk family and do not reach for a light ground until the counted window holds none.

A FRAME COMPUTED ITS OWN GEOMETRY AND FOUR SCORING PANELS DID NOT SEE IT. slide-05.html drew its plot at 180 px per day while compute.py held 300, so every y coordinate computed.json published for that frame described a plot nobody drew. slide-04.html held run_depth 138 and run_gap 178 against computed.json's 96 and 190, under a comment reading FROM compute.py. Both were hand-synced literals. The fix is to INJECT each slide's computed block into its frame rather than retyping it, and it is in the backlog as a proposal.

THE RUN CORRECTED THE RECORD TOWARD THE WRONG HALF. A judge reported aggregates.json declaring 180 against computed.json's 300 and the run changed the declaration to 300 with a confident paragraph attached. 300 was the number nobody drew. When two files disagree about a drawing, MEASURE THE RENDER before deciding which one is stale.

A REPAIR CAN BE WORSE THAN THE DEFECT AND ONLY THE THUMB WILL SAY SO. Round 4 put a lit sill slab under the cover's doorway to stop it reading as a hole in a wall, and a sill is the most window-defining element in architecture, so all three judges then read the cover as a window. Round 5's ambient fix on slide 6 clipped its own gradient and rendered two translucent boxes. Read every repair at 432px against the defect it was meant to cure.

THREE UNSOURCED STRINGS REACHED FRAMES AND NO GATE COULD SEE ANY OF THEM. OPEN ACCESS AND FREE TO READ TODAY on slide 9, an unlicensed universal on slide 2, and a cover dek making the hospital the subject of both compared and published when c1 places only the encounters there and c14 names the journal. Each was found by a human-style read of pixels against claims.json. The gate that would catch the class extracts the SUBJECT and main verb of every declarative sentence and checks that subject is an agent of that act inside a cited claim's quote.

A BANNED PHRASE SHIPPED TO TWO SURFACES BEHIND A GREEN caption_check. brand.yaml lists actionable in banned_phrases and caption_check.py does not read that key at all. Same shape as the light cap: a rule stated in config with nothing in between checking it.
SLIDE 9 IS THE THINNEST FRAME FOR THE FIFTH CONSECUTIVE DECK, which decks 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 each wrote down and none has paid. Draw the close FIRST next time.

THE TYPE MOVED ON THREE FRAMES AND IT MOVED IN ROUND 3. Deck 15 asked for three moves PLANNED IN THE STORYBOARD rather than repaired late, and two of the three here are right-alignment, the cheapest move on the shelf.

entries.register: A CALICHE TWO-TRACK ON THE EDWARDS PLATEAU WEST OF AUSTIN, TWENTY MINUTES AFTER SUNSET. One grazing key from the west at 4 degrees above grade, declared once in compute.py and read by every relief call and every shadow solver on all nine frames. The defining chromatic move is a WARM-COOL SPLIT ACROSS ONE MATERIAL: road base in direct last light is rose, and the same stone under the dome only is violet-grey. Deck 18 had no key and therefore no split. Deck 19 was midday.
structural_laws: WHAT IS IN FORCE IS DRAWN. WHAT IS PROPOSED IS ONLY TYPE. The Department of Transportation's proposal appears on frames 4 and 7 and is never given a body, a shadow or a lit surface, so the deck structurally cannot predict.

ATTRIBUTION. A party's own statement is a SHEET LAID ON THE GROUND with a declared two-part contact shadow. The agency's record is set into the frame with no carrier. Sheets exist on frames 3, 6 and 8 and nowhere else.

NO VANISHING POINT AND NO VEHICLE IN ANY OF NINE FRAMES. Not one camera sits where a driver would. This discharges the deck's hard editorial constraint as GEOMETRY rather than as wording, which is the only form of it a repair round cannot argue away.
techniques: s1 Big Bend dusk field over a wire-relief rut heightfield, the camera looking ACROSS the two-track so the ruts are two troughs and nothing converges
s2 a measured field table over an unlit ground, with an engraved intaglio bed carrying the bottom third, which is form without any key light on a frame that has none
s3 TXCARVE wind-worked road base with a two-part contact under a cool sheet and a cobble
s4 norther front over wire relief on a shut wire gap gate whose four wires carry the four controls the standards assume, counted from c10's own list
s5 stipple at 3 degrees grazing incidence across the first pass of one tyre in loose dust
s6 an untruncated ground dimension whose TERMINATOR WIDTHS are the record's own precision, a full year wide at 2022 and one month wide at July 2026
s7 a hachure field driven from the same rut heightfield's real gradient, lifting toward the foot against a ground that darkens
s8 an engraved contour bed under two plates from one constant set, no ground and no light
s9 true plan, straight down, wire relief over a rut heightfield, with a cattle guard cropped at both frame edges so no rail total is countable

entries.type_skeletons: FIVE across nine, planned in the storyboard rather than repaired in a scoring round. A on 1, 5, 9. B, a field table with no hook where the top rule is the head, on 2 and 6. C, one shared measure with a hanging indent, on 3 and 8. D, display type at the deck's largest size filling the top band, on 4. E, four flush-left lines at one size as a single mass, on 7. Right-alignment is used nowhere as a substitute for a layout decision.

avoid_next: THE DECK MAY GO LIGHT AGAIN AND THE COUNTED WINDOW IS WHY. Decks 14 and 19 were the two light decks in the eight-run window and this one at deck median 18.1 clears the debt. Check the window before choosing, and MEASURE the deck median rather than asserting it, which is what deck 19 got wrong by miscounting its own ledger twice.

A GATE NOBODY RUNS IS A GATE THAT IS RED. construction_check.py is not in guards.yml and is not named in the routine's phase list, so this run reached scoring round 3 before it was run once, and it was red the whole time at 5 of 9 frames carrying one primitive against a threshold of half. The four decks before this one measured 2, 1, 4 and 1, so the finding was real rather than a drifted threshold. Run every gate in scripts/carousel by exit code before the first panel, not the ones the routine happens to list.

A REPORT THAT PREDATES THE ARTIFACT IT DESCRIBES READS AS NO CHANGE AT ALL. panel_ready takes its contrast numbers from machine_qa.json, and on this run that file was seven minutes older than the PNGs, so a whole round of colour fixes measured as nothing. qa.py now runs inside build.sh on every render. Before believing any report, check its mtime against the newest artifact it reads.

putImageData IGNORES THE CANVAS TRANSFORM. A scanline written after g.scale(2,2) lands in a quadrant, and the frame comes back at a fifth of its planned value with zero render errors. Write the field at device resolution and put it once.

THE SECOND REPAIR OF A FRAME IS WHERE THE DECK'S OWN LAW GETS BROKEN. This cover's second build gave the ruts the slight convergence a long lens really has, and the frame immediately read as the view down a road from a driver's seat, which is the one thing this deck's first structural law forbids. Director C had named that exact repair in advance as one to refuse at the plan. Read every repair against the LAW, not only against the defect it was meant to cure.

DECLARE A PALETTE TOKEN AND THEN DRAW IT. plan_render_check found three declared tokens no frame contained as a literal, on three separate frames, and the plan and the frames had drifted apart in twelve places in total by the first full render.
SLIDE 9 WAS DRAWN FIRST AND IT STILL TOOK TWO REBUILDS AFTER THAT. Drawing the close first is necessary and it is not sufficient. Budget a rebuild for it anyway.
